## Strongest exact statement

Deterministic independent replay validates the protected predecessor claim without modification. For every valid weighted-two-color-blowup-v1 certificate with m blocks, positive weights w_1,...,w_m, total weight Q=sum_i w_i, and exact ordered-four-tuple monochromatic density P from the protected packet, one has P >= sum_i (w_i/Q)^4 >= 1/m^3. Hence every certificate with m <= 3 satisfies P >= 1/27.

The bound is sharp over the full m <= 3 class. For m=3, weights [1,1,1] with red_rows ["100","010","001"] have exact red numerator 3, blue numerator 0, denominator 81, and P=1/27; the color complement ["011","101","110"] has red numerator 0, blue numerator 3, denominator 81, and the same density. The frozen reference is B*=10486266368/768^4=20480989/679477248, and 1/27-B*=4684835/679477248>0. Therefore no certificate with at most three blocks beats the frozen reference, so every reference-beating certificate in this schema must use at least four blocks.

## Derivation

Let A be the symmetric 0-1 block-color matrix. In the exact ordered four-tuple expansion, the contribution of a tuple (a,b,c,d) is its weight product multiplied by the indicator that all six pair colors are red or all six are blue. For every pure diagonal tuple (i,i,i,i), all six pairs equal (i,i). If A_ii=1 the red indicator is 1 and the blue indicator is 0; if A_ii=0 the red indicator is 0 and the blue indicator is 1. Thus every block contributes w_i^4 to the numerator regardless of diagonal color.

All remaining ordered tuples contribute nonnegative mass, so P >= (sum_i w_i^4)/Q^4 = sum_i (w_i/Q)^4. Since x^4 is convex and sum_i w_i/Q=1, Jensen's inequality gives sum_i (w_i/Q)^4 >= 1/m^3. For m<=3 this implies P>=1/27.

For sharpness, take m=3 with equal weights and red diagonal, blue off-diagonal. Any ordered four-tuple using at least two block labels has both a repeated-label pair and an unequal-label pair because four distinct labels are impossible with only three blocks. Those two pair types have opposite colors, so such a tuple is not monochromatic. Only the three pure diagonal tuples survive, giving numerator 3 and denominator 81.

An independent exhaustive symbolic replay enumerated every symmetric binary matrix for m=1,2,3 by upper-triangular bits, expanded every ordered four-tuple into its sorted weight-monomial label, and counted a coefficient exactly when its six pair colors were all 1 or all 0. The replay covered 2+8+64=74 matrices. In every case the coefficient of each pure diagonal monomial w_i^4 was exactly 1 and every cross-monomial coefficient was nonnegative. Cross terms vanished identically for exactly two matrices at m=2, namely ["01","10"] and ["10","01"], and exactly two matrices at m=3, namely ["011","101","110"] and ["100","010","001"], agreeing with the complementary extremizers.
